codeReview.summary: Clean, focused implementation that adds evaluator invocation to the execution loop with proper guard conditions. The change is minimal and surgical — only 62 lines added to execution-loop.ts (1 import + evaluator block) plus 614 lines of comprehensive tests. The implementation correctly instantiates the Evaluator class after successful phase execution, passes the right inputs (workerOutput, validation_criteria, context_files, durationSeconds), handles pass/fail/skip outcomes, and emits appropriate events. All guard conditions (no transport, skip_evaluation, no decision, no validation_criteria) are properly checked. The Evaluator class handles timeout graceful degradation internally, so the execution loop correctly treats skipped results as passing. Code follows existing project conventions (Log module for logging, emitter for events, statePersistence for state updates).

issues.description: The skipEvaluation parameter passed to the Evaluator constructor is always false at this point, because the outer guard already checks !this.config.skip_evaluation. While not a bug (it's a redundant safety net), it adds a tiny amount of unnecessary indirection. The Evaluator class's internal skip check will never trigger through this code path.

When evaluation fails, the phase state is set back to 'pending' via statePersistence.updatePhase(), but then the loop returns immediately with completed:false. This means a failed evaluation leaves the phase in 'pending' state even though the workflow has terminated. A more precise status might be 'failed', but this follows the existing pattern where phase-executor retries set status to 'pending' for retry, and since the workflow terminates here anyway, the semantic difference is minimal.

The timeout graceful degradation test relies on the Evaluator class's internal timeout handling (TimeoutError catch → skipped:true return). The test transport simulates timeout via setTimeout(reject, 10ms). This works correctly but tests the Evaluator class's timeout handling rather than the execution loop's handling of it — the loop's role is just to check !evalResult.passed && !evalResult.skipped, which is tested. This is fine for integration-level coverage.

summary: PASS. The implementation correctly activates the dormant evaluator in the execution loop. The change is minimal (62 lines in production code) and well-tested (18 tests covering all guard conditions, pass/fail/timeout paths, event emission, multi-phase execution, config flow, and backward compatibility). All 6 validation assertions (VAL-EVALACT-001 through VAL-EVALACT-006) are fulfilled: evaluator is invoked after phase completion with correct inputs (001), phase fails on passed=false with reason (002), skip_evaluation config bypasses evaluator (003), timeout degrades gracefully (004), missing validation_criteria skips evaluator (005), and evaluator events are emitted for TUI rendering (006). No blocking issues found. Three non-blocking observations noted: redundant skipEvaluation parameter, phase state set to 'pending' on evaluation failure, and timeout test testing Evaluator internals rather than loop behavior — all are minor and don't affect correctness.
